title: Performance of multiclass Markovian queueing networks
contribution: Shows that linear and piecewise linear Lyapunov functions that certify stability of multiclass Markovian queueing networks also give geometric-type upper and lower tail bounds on queue lengths, hence bounds on their expectation; e.g. E[L] = O(1/(1-rho*)^2) for a two-station re-entrant line under any work-conserving policy (abstract).
problem_entry: {SD} Steady-state queue-length distribution under a stable policy; entry: earlier results gave numerical bounds, and only on the expectation, not the distribution (abstract).
key_idea: Reuse the stability certificate (a linear or piecewise linear Lyapunov function) to bound tail probabilities geometrically (abstract).
assumptions: Markovian multiclass queueing networks under a stable policy; general Markovian and priority policies also treated (abstract).
proof_devices: Lyapunov-function methodology for infinite-state Markov chains: the functions that show stability yield geometric-type tail bounds (abstract)
positioning: Extends Dai and Vande-Vate's stability result for two-station re-entrant lines (rho* < 1) to explicit performance bounds (abstract).
writing: Ends with a priority claim and names what earlier results lacked (numerical bounds on the expectation only) (abstract).
limits_future: Limits not stated in the abstract. Journal version: S123 (Ann. Appl. Probab. 2001, card s05).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: stability certificate reused as a performance bound
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Lyapunov functions that show stability give geometric tail bounds and expectation bounds (existing name, card s05 for the journal version S123)

transferable: When a Lyapunov (drift) certificate of stability exists, try to extract geometric tail bounds from the same function before building a new performance argument (abstract).

quotes.text: We establish a deeper connection between stability and performance of such networks by showing that if there exist linear and piecewise linear Lyapunov functions that show stability, then these Lyapunov functions can be used to establish geometric type lower and upper bounds on the tail probabilities, and thus bounds on the expectation of the queue lengths.
Previous results provide numerical bounds and only on the expectation, not the distribution, of queue lengths.

title: Multistage air traffic flow management under capacity uncertainty: a robust and adaptive optimization approach
contribution: First application of robust and adaptive optimization to network air traffic flow management under weather-induced capacity uncertainty: a low-dimensional weather-front uncertainty set, a polyhedral description of its convex hull, the robust problem as a modified deterministic instance, and the LP relaxation of the adaptive problem solved by piecewise affine policies (often affine suffices); on real schedules with simulated fronts the robust problem keeps integrality and speed and the price of robustness and adaptability is typically small (abstract).

experiments: Real-world flight schedules with simulated weather fronts; the robust problem keeps the integrality properties and run times of the deterministic one; the price of robustness and adaptability is typically small (abstract).
positioning: Claims the first application of robust and adaptive optimization to ATFM; existing network models are deterministic (abstract).

quotes.text: In this paper, we study the first application of robust and adaptive optimization in the Air Traffic Flow Management (ATFM) problem.

The key insights from our computational results are: i) the robust problem inherits all the attractive properties of the deterministic problem (e.g., superior integrality properties and fast computational times); and ii) the price of robustness and adaptability is typically small.
